R7BI-bear-walk-0003.name: By Niloil Creek
R7BI-bear-walk-0003.pressureWhy: 4.7 km on foot from the nearest parking inside a motor vehicle closure (estimate).
R7BI-bear-walk-0003.parkWhat: pull off on Hwy 97 (Alaska Hwy) (paved road)

evidence.t: Burn from 2023 (fire G90949), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 15 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Niloil Creek 40 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

flags.t: Spot is inside a Motor Vehicle Closed Area: Muskwa-Kechika Access Management Area. Closed Year Round. Synopsis map 1-114/26.

plan: Drive: from Northern Rockies Regional Municipality, about 278 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 59.62286, -127.0576, pull off on Hwy 97 (Alaska Hwy) (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 4.7 km S, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 156 m, about 109 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-51, Region 7B. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2024-10-05, closures 2026-10-16.
R7BI-bear-walk-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 7-51: about 100 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.01 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: a long walk from parking. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

evidence.t: 9 wetlands within 2 km; nearest 4.2 ha, right here.
Burn from 2023 (fire G90949), right here: browse.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

seasonRows.cls: Spike fork, tripalm or 10 point bulls
seasonRows.notes: Bag 1. 7-43 portion only (LEH Synopsis map 7P, printed green); portion of 7-51 closed (Map H32); 7-52 portion only (LEH Synopsis map 7R)
LEH (Limited Entry Hunting): draw only, not a general open season

plan: Drive: from Northern Rockies Regional Municipality, about 278 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).

Walk: 2.3 km S, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 85 m, about 55 min at 3 km/h.
Hunt: moose, Sept, Oct (season rows). Glass the wetland and cutblock edges at dawn and dusk. Move slowly, stop often (Tip).
Use: .308 Winchester, 165 to 180 grain premium bullet, shots inside about 200 m (219 yd) (Tip).
